text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 alert: GPU pod gpupool-12-job-442 reported NCCL timeout during TP forward. Multiple replicas failing rendezvous (tensor-parallel). Paged oncall.

sre_kate: I'm on it. Which cluster and which customer? any recent deploys?

eng-ml-jun: Cluster: prod-us-west-2-a, node set gpu-a5. Customer: AcmeGames realtime-inference (low-latency). No recent rollout for that model in the last 6h.

chris: seeing repeated container restarts on pod gpupool-12-job-442, crashloop with SIGABRT in runtime. Logs show CUDA driver error before crash.

maya: marking impacted sessions: ~120 active requests failing with 500s, latency spikes. Support: pinged Acme via incident channel.

ops_raj: checking node level: `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep gpupool-12` shows pods on node gpu-a5-03 and gpu-a5-07 flapping.

eng-ml-jun: paste of diagnostic logs:
```
[2026-03-15T08:12:11Z] NCCL INFO Comm id recv timed out, status=UNREACHABLE
[2026-03-15T08:12:11Z] NCCL WARN TX failed on rank 1 -> rank 3
[2026-03-15T08:12:11Z] CUDA Error: all CUDA-capable devices are busy or unavailable
```

sre_kate: run `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,POWER` and `dmesg | tail -n 50` on gpu-a5-03. Also get `docker logs --since 5m gpupool-12-job-442`.

ops_raj: nvidia-smi output: GPU0 killed (ECC errors) on gpu-a5-03, memory corruption reported. dmesg shows `NVRM: Xid 79: GPU has fallen off the bus` repeatedly.

samir: that Xid 79 indicates a GPU reset. Could be a driver/hw fault causing NCCL communicator to lose peers -> rendezvous freeze.

eng-ml-jun: temporary mitigation: can we drain the two affected nodes and failover traffic to a lower-capacity pool? we should avoid OOM-driven retries.

chris: initiating cordon/drain on gpu-a5-03 and gpu-a5-07. `kubectl cordon gpu-a5-03 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-a5-03` — will move pods but TP jobs may not checkpoint.

maya: Support update sent to AcmeGames: "We're investigating GPU hardware resets causing multi-GPU jobs to fail. Mitigation in progress; you may see degraded throughput for ~15-30m. Will update every 10m." :email:

oncall-bot: @oncall (today) paged for SEV-2: sre_kate

sre_kate: I'll run a targeted fallback: route new requests for Acme model to fallback-model:v2-quant (single-GPU) to reduce multi-GPU rendezvous pressure. Updating routing policy now.

eng-ml-jun: Can confirm routing change applied: AcmeGames -> fallback-model:v2-quant. Telemetry: p99 latency increased by ~40ms but failure rate dropped to 2%.

support-emma: logging incident in Incident Tracker (#INC-2026-231). Severity: SEV-2, customer-impacting. ETA for full remediation depends on hardware replacement or driver rollback.

samir: Suggested durable fix: disable continuous KV cache prefetch for TP jobs temporarily and add keepalive probe to NCCL to detect earlier and failfast.

chris: container logs show CUDA runtime abort right before crash:
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  CUDA failed: unspecified launch failure (an illegal memory access was encountered)
```

ops_raj: I'm opening a hardware ticket with the cloud provider for gpu-a5-03. Also collecting core dumps: `/var/crash/gpupool-12-job-442` archived to s3://redwood-cores/2345678910/

sre_kate: handoff to hardware oncall: @raj you're owning node remediation. I'll stay on until failover is stable and customer updated.

ops_raj: acknowledged. node repair ticket ID CP-948281 created.

maya: update for Exec: Impacted calls peaked 180rps failing; now reduced to ~8rps failing after routing change. Customers in GA region only.

eng-ml-jun: postmortem notes to capture: (1) detect GPU Xid 79 earlier via pc-side monitoring, (2) automated quick-fallback to single-GPU model, (3) add NCCL keepalive and failfast config for TP workloads.

sre_kate: saving thread context and adding to incident doc. Next update in 10m or earlier if node repair completes.

incident-bot: Incident pinned to channel. Severity set to SEV-2. Timeline started at 2345678910.

chris: one last note — avoid mass restarts; we saw cascading OOMs when pods attempted to reschedule on same node pool. Use staggered restart policy.

support-emma: notifying account manager for AcmeGames now.

sre_kate: handing off to night oncall at 2345678975. Night oncall, please monitor Acme's request rate and hardware ticket. I'm leaving actionable runbook in the incident doc. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. New oncall: samir.

samir: ack, taking over. Will follow up on hardware ticket and ensure fallback stays active. Will post a summary and recommended mitigations in the incident doc.

support-emma: customer update sent: "We have mitigated the immediate failures by routing you to a lower-latency fallback. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline for node repair."
